description: Every update from every ecosystem lands in one PR on Monday morning: crates, the Rust toolchain, GitHub Actions, and the Python requirements, re-resolved by uv rather than moved pin by pin. Vulnerability fixes ride in it too rather than as PRs of their own; everything is taken to its latest version, so a vulnerable version never survives the week.

Cargo's transitive dependencies are the one thing that cannot join it: Renovate refuses to group a lock file refresh with other update types, so `cargo update` arrives as a second PR on Tuesday, after Monday's has had a day to be merged.
A release has to be three days old before it is offered, which is the cheapest defence there is against a package taken over the day it is published.

packageRules.description: The manifests name the versions the binary is built with, so an in-range update moves the manifest as well as the lock rather than leaving the two to drift apart.

A runner image this datasource knows about is not the same as a label GitHub will schedule a job on: gdharness was offered ubuntu-26.04 while the labels stopped at ubuntu-24.04, and the raise failed actionlint on every workflow. Moving to a new image is a decision to make once the label exists, not one to take again every week, and for the release build it changes the machine every binary is made on.

A digest update is aged at lookup against the release its tag resolves to, but the branch's stability check reads a timestamp field digest updates never carry, and a lock file refresh has no release to age at all. Left at the default, every pinned action held the one combined PR at pending for good. Optional still ages whatever does carry a timestamp.

Held until a dynamo-exported graph runs on DirectML. Training is fine on transformers 5, but half precision through the TorchScript exporter writes a graph whose LayerNormalization takes one float input and one half one, which onnxruntime refuses to load. The dynamo exporter writes a graph that loads, keeps its weights in one file and agrees with the model to 8.75e-03 with no answer changed, and then fails on a Reshape node inside the DirectML provider four seconds into a read the traced graph does at 909 claims a second. Measured 2026-09-14; DECISIONS records it.

huggingface_hub 1 is what transformers 5 wants, and it goes when transformers goes. Both spellings, because PyPI normalises the underscore to a hyphen and the lock file writes the underscore: matched on the underscore alone, the rule never fired and the Monday PR offered 1.32 against a transformers that refuses it.
tokenizers follows transformers: 4.57 will not take 0.23.

pip_requirements.description: Off. requirements.txt holds loose floors by hand, and moving a pin in the lock one line at a time is what offered mpmath 1.4 against a sympy that refuses it: this manager has no resolver, and nothing here is its to edit.

pip-compile.description: requirements.lock is `uv pip compile` over requirements.txt, and the command that made it is in the file's header. Every update is a re-run of that command with the one package raised, and lock file maintenance is a re-run with everything raised, so a pin is never moved past what another pin allows. The header carries only the source and the output file: Renovate refuses any option it does not know, and the index, platform and Python version the lock is resolved for live in the root uv.toml, which uv reads from the directory the command runs in.

customManagers.description: A tool the workflows download with the SHA-256 of the file they fetch on the next line: actionlint and syft. The tag and the digest move together, and the datasource finds the new digest in the checksum file the release publishes.
The runner images inside the release build's matrix, which the github-actions manager reads from runs-on: but not from a matrix.
